title: Refined quasi-finite affine-space chart with purely transcendental image residue field
statement: Let $p:Z\to S$ be a finite type morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $z\in Z$, put $s=p(z)$, and set $n=\dim_z(Z_s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-dimension]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $S_0\subseteq S$ of $s$ and $Z_0\subseteq p^{-1}(S_0)$ of $z$, and an $S_0$-morphism $q:Z_0\to\mathbf A^n_{S_0}$ [def-sbc-affine-space], such that $q$ is quasi-finite (of finite type with finite discrete fibres) and, for $t=q(z)$, the induced extension $\kappa(t)/\kappa(s)$ is purely transcendental: it is isomorphic over $\kappa(s)$ to $\kappa(s)(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ for some $0\le r\le n$. The dimension here is topological dimension at the point, not the dimension of its local ring.

source.place: Tag 0520, lemma-refined-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, and its scheme translation in more-morphisms.tex Tag 052E, first paragraph of proof. The prime in the polynomial algebra is (p,x_{r+1},...,x_n), hence has residue field kappa(p)(x_1,...,x_r).

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $\mathfrak q_A$ represent $z$ with contraction $\mathfrak p$. Denote the induced ring map by $\rho:R\to A$; the affine-pairs finite-type criterion makes it finite type. The affine fibre formula and fibre-prime correspondence identify $Z_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ and its marked prime. The affine coordinate fibre-dimension comparison identifies its dimension with $n$. The fibre ring $A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finitely generated $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra (the images $a_i\otimes1$ of generators of $A$ over $R$ generate it), so $Z_s$ is of finite type over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives $\dim Z_s<\infty$; since $Z_s$ is itself an open neighbourhood of $z$, $n=\dim_z(Z_s)\le\dim Z_s$ is a natural number, as the polynomial-chart lemma requires. Apply the polynomial-chart lemma to obtain $g\notin\mathfrak q_A$ and a finite type, everywhere quasi-finite $\alpha:R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to A_g$.

Put $\mathfrak q_B=\mathfrak q_A A_g$ and $\mathfrak q'=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q_B)$. Since $\alpha$ is an $R$-algebra map, localization extension-contraction gives $\mathfrak q'\cap R=\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q_A)=\mathfrak p$. Apply [lem-trf-normalized-polynomial-prime-lift] to $R,\mathfrak q'$: obtain $0\le r\le n$, $f\notin\mathfrak p$, and $\psi:C=R_f[x]\to D=R_f[t]$, finite type with finite special-fibre map and $P=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q'D)=(\mathfrak pR_f,x_{r+1},\ldots,x_n)$.

source.place: Tag 0520, normalized lifted coordinates and prescribed inverse-image prime

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-fibre-synchronized-chart-shrink] to $\alpha$ and $\psi$. The marked primes and their contractions are those fixed in steps 1 and 2. The map $\rho$ is finite type by step 1; $\alpha$ is finite type and everywhere quasi-finite, and step 2 supplies $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and the finite type map $\psi$ with finite special fibre. It gives $d=g\rho(f)a\notin\mathfrak q_A$ and a finite type, everywhere quasi-finite $\theta:C\to A_d$ with $\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak q_A A_d)=P$; the image of $f$ is a unit in $A_d$.

source.place: Tag 0520, finite-fibre shrinking and localized composition

proof.text: Under the affine identifications of step 1, apply [lem-trf-coordinate-prime-affine-chart-realization] to $R\to A$, $f,d,r,n,\theta$, viewed as an $R_f$-algebra map as supplied in step 3. It gives affine neighbourhoods $S_0=D(f)$ and $Z_0=D(d)\subseteq p^{-1}(S_0)$ and the required $S_0$-morphism $q:Z_0\to\mathbf A^n_{S_0}$, of finite type with finite discrete fibres. Its image-point residue field is $\kappa(s)(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ over $\kappa(s)$. The integer $n$ is still the original topological fibre dimension from step 1, and $0\le r\le n$ comes from step 2.
